comms.spawn_traffic_off: Other traffic is switched off in Settings.

comms.spawn_not_in_sim: The simulator is not creating AI aircraft, so none can be put on the runway.
comms.spawn_failed: Could not put an aircraft on the runway.
comms.debug_board_why: Testing: the parked aircraft nearest you starts boarding now
comms.debug_arrival_why: Testing: an arrival on short final to the free stand nearest you
comms.debug_no_free_stand: No free stand for an arrival.
comms.debug_failed: That cannot be done right now.
strip.title: Flight strip
map.aria: Airports and controller positions around the aircraft
map.view3d_title: The airport in 3D when you zoom in. Drag with the right button, or with Shift, to turn and tilt it.
craft.heading: Heading
wx.title: Weather
freq.search: an airport code, a frequency, or a position
atis.hint: Tune a field with an ATIS and its wording appears here.
set.ui_language_why: What this window is written in. It does not change what is spoken on the radio, which follows the aeroplane.
set.radio_effects_why: The band-limited AM channel, not the raw voice
set.operator_why: A controller is somebody in a room, not a file being played. They take a moment after keying up, they are never quite the same loudness twice, and once in a while they say “uh”.
set.breathing_why: An audible breath in the gaps of a long clearance
set.wind_why: Wind gusting under the voice, the way an open tower cab sounds
set.hesitation_why: The occasional “uh” before the callsign. Rare on purpose.
set.button_why: Press the one you want to talk on. Nobody publishes which number a yoke calls its buttons.
set.ptt_why: Use one the simulator does not need. The panel's own button works either way.
set.no_controller_found: no controller connected — plug one in and reopen this screen
set.controller_offline: Known to this computer but not connected: {names}
set.spoken_language_why: Follows the aeroplane. English everywhere, plus the local language over a state that works one. Speak either; the controller answers in the one you used.
set.handoffs_why: Name the next frequency when you outfly this one
set.simbrief_why: Fill the flight in from your latest plan instead of typing it twice.
set.simbrief_no_user: Put your SimBrief username in Settings first.
set.ground_why: No taxi clearance while the tug or the jetway is still attached
set.ground_call_why: An approved pushback calls one, through GSX’s own menu
set.ground_voice_why: “Ground crew, request pushback” — and boarding, fuel, catering or de-icing
set.traffic_why: Airlines that belong at this field, each crew in its own language
set.traffic_gsx_why: With GSX Pro installed, its stairs, loaders, caterers and tugs serve the other aircraft. Off: the simulator's own vehicles
set.traffic_callsigns_why: Airline callsigns are what a large field really carries; registrations are easier to follow, because you hear the letters rather than a name you have to know.
set.real_obs_why: METARs from the NOAA Aviation Weather Center
set.sim_wins_why: Custom weather in the sim has to match the ATIS
set.sim_stand_in: no simulator — flying on a stand-in position
set.rules_plus: Understanding: rules, with {model} for anything they miss.
set.saved_restart: saved — restart WilcoATC for this to take effect
log.traffic_visible: Traffic will be visible in the simulator.
log.traffic_observed: Working {count} aircraft from the simulator's own traffic.
log.traffic_spawned_holding: {callsign} is holding short of runway {runway} until the runway is free.
log.traffic_spawn_failed: The simulator could not create {callsign}, so it is not on the runway.
log.placed: No simulator, so placing the aircraft at {airport}.
log.callsign_heard: Callsign {callsign}, as said on the radio (was {was}, from {source}).
log.bilingual: {where}: {language} is worked here alongside English. Speak either; the controller answers in the one you used.
log.ptt: Push to talk: hold the {key_name} key.
log.ptt_button: Push to talk: hold joystick {stick} button {button}.
log.tuned_advisory: {mhz} — {station}: an advisory frequency, so nobody answers. Announce your position and listen out.
log.human_online: {mhz} — {station} is working this frequency on {network}. WilcoATC will stay quiet on it.
log.empty_frequency: {mhz} — nobody is listening on this frequency at {field}. Published there: {listing}.
log.empty_frequency_near: {mhz} — nobody is listening on this frequency at {field}. Published there: {listing}. Did you mean {near} ({station})?
log.empty_frequency_alone: {mhz} — nobody is listening on this frequency here.
log.still_working: Still working on the last transmission.
log.nobody_listening: No station is listening on this frequency.
log.transmit_stuck: The transmit button has been down for {seconds} seconds, so the transmission was ended. Nothing else could be said while it was.
log.cabin_no_audio: The cabin and the first officer cannot reach the speaker. The radio is unaffected. ({detail})
log.crew_no_voice: The crew cannot be synthesised, so the cabin is silent. The radio is unaffected. ({detail})
log.announcements_missing: No announcements folder called "{folder}". The cabin is using its own voices.
log.announcements_empty: Recorded announcements are switched on, but no audio files were found. The cabin is using its own voices.
log.unpublished: {mhz} is not in the published data for {airport}. Answering as {station}. To keep it: {command}
notice.title: This is alpha software
notice.body: WilcoATC is in alpha. You will run into bugs, and you will run into a lot of them.
notice.point1: The controller can say the wrong thing, or something that makes no sense at all.
notice.point2: It can fail to understand you, or hear something you never said.
notice.point3: Anything here can change or stop working from one version to the next.
notice.agree: I know what I am getting into, and I am using this at my own risk.
flight.title: Flight
flight.why: The simulator supplies your position and radios. These are the details it cannot tell us.
order.touch_and_go_discretion: touch and go at its discretion
order.heading: heading
log.departure_moved: The aircraft is at {airport}, not {was}. Using {airport}.
log.sim_lost: Lost the simulator. Looking for it again.
log.sim_waiting: Simulator not detected. Waiting for it, and flying from the manually set aircraft state until it appears.
log.type_moved: The simulator has a {type}, not a {was}.
map.follow_title: Keep the map on the aircraft
map.no_controller: no controller within range of you
set.copilot_why: Callouts, checklists and the numbers read back to you
set.callouts_why: Eighty knots, V one, rotate, positive rate, and the calls on the way down
set.confirmations_why: Says the numbers back to you on the interphone, so two of you heard them
set.checklists_why: Called and answered at the points a flight actually runs them
set.readbacks_why: Reads a clearance back if you have not, after a few seconds. Off unless you want it: the point of the radio is usually to work it yourself.
set.cabin_crew_why: A purser and a cabin, on the address system
set.briefings_why: The demonstration during the taxi out, and the crew calls around it
set.announcements_why: Welcome aboard, the cruise, the descent, and where you have arrived
set.service_why: The trolley after the climb, and a call to the flight deck before it
set.chimes_why: The two notes before an announcement, and the seatbelt sign
set.boarding_music_why: Plays quietly in the cabin while people get on, and stops at pushback
set.crew_manner: Who they are, and how much
set.airline_name: What the crew call the airline
set.airline_why: Left empty, they take it from your callsign, and say “this flight” for a private registration.
set.captain_name_why: Left empty, one is cast from the registration, and the same aeroplane keeps the same captain.
set.talk_to_crew_why: Say “cabin crew” or “ground crew” first, and they answer instead of the controller
set.use_sim: Take the aircraft from the simulator
set.use_sim_why: Off, the aeroplane sits where you put it and nothing moves
log.traffic_refused: This simulator will not create AI aircraft, so WilcoATC adds no traffic of its own. Aircraft already in the simulator are still worked.
set.use_recordings_why: A real announcement beats a synthesised one. Where a recording exists for a moment, it is played instead.
set.announcements_dir_why: Leave it empty to use the folder beside WilcoATC, or point it at a pack you already have. The layout is the one the Fenix A320 uses, so a pack made for that aeroplane works in any of them.
set.components_why: The voices, the nav database and the speech recogniser are too big to ship with the program, so they are downloaded once. About 1.5 GB in total.
set.data_credits: Enroute sectors: VatGlasses contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
setup.title: Getting the pieces
setup.why: Three things are too big to ship inside the program and are downloaded once: the voices your controllers speak with, the database of every airport and frequency, and the model that hears you. About 1.5 GB, and you only do this once.
setup.retry: Something did not download. Check the connection and try again: what already arrived is kept.
setup.leave_open: You can close this and carry on. The download keeps going.
setup.extra_voices_why: 2.3 GB more. Controllers abroad speak English with their own country's accent; without it they use a neutral British voice.
setup.hq_voices_why: 2 GB more. The most natural voices, but slow without a graphics card: a long clearance can take a minute to arrive.
setup.vatglasses_licence: Made by the VatGlasses contributors and shared under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: for non-commercial use only. Downloaded on its own, never part of WilcoATC. Without it, centre calls use the published boundaries.
setup.restart: Downloaded. Restart WilcoATC to use it.
doctor.title: Diagnostics
doctor.why: The same check wilcoatc doctor runs in a terminal: every part of the program, whether it is there, and what it found.
log.voices_missing: The controller voices have not been downloaded yet. Open Settings, then Components, and press Download.
log.hq_missing: The cloned voices are not installed, so the controllers are using the standard voices. Download the cloning model with: {command}
alert.no_voices: The controllers have no voice yet
setup.ready: Downloaded. The controllers have their voices.
log.no_enroute_frequency: No enroute frequency is published for this area ({sector}). Staying with the radar controller you are on. Add one with: {command} <ICAO> --add CTR <frequency> --name <name>
set.applause_why: The cabin claps when you touch down gentler than 200 feet per minute
set.landing_report_why: A few seconds after touchdown: the landing rate, how smooth it was, and the flight against its SimBrief schedule
tour.welcome_text: Air traffic control for your flight, running on this computer. Tune a frequency in COM1, hold your push-to-talk key, speak, and the controller answers. This tour takes about a minute.
tour.screens_text: Comms is where you talk. Airspace is the map, Frequencies the list of who you can call, and Settings everything else.
tour.transcript_text: Everything said on the frequency, by you and by the controllers, in the order it was said.
tour.talk_text: Hold your push-to-talk key and speak; release it to send. You can also type what you would say and press Enter. The key is chosen in Settings, Push to talk.
tour.phrases_text: Suggestions for where you are in the flight. Click one to send it as it is.
tour.station_text: The frequency in COM1 and who answers on it. Below it, the standby frequency and the button that swaps the two, as the radio in the cockpit does.
tour.strip_text: Callsign, aircraft, squawk, runway and route, as the controllers know them. The pencil changes them, and your SimBrief plan can fill them in.
tour.airspace_text: Airports, the stations whose frequencies reach you, and the other traffic. Zoom in close to a field and it becomes a 3D model of the airport.
tour.frequencies_text: Every published frequency within reach, nearest first. Click one to tune it in COM1, in the aircraft as well.
tour.settings_text: The voices, the microphone and the push-to-talk key, the look of this window and more. This tour can be shown again from Interface.
tour.done_text: Start the simulator, find the frequency of your airport under Frequencies, tune it and make your first call. Have a good flight.
set.tour_why: The short walk round this window that opens on the first launch
landing.title: Landing report
landing.no_plan: Load a SimBrief plan to compare this flight against its schedule.
set.crew_realism_why: A little interphone and cabin speaker on their voices, and the odd um and er
set.bilingual_why: A crew whose language is not English repeat each cabin announcement in English
set.look_why: Colours, background and glass. Everything changes as you pick it, the icon included.
set.look_theme_why: Dark for night flights, light for the day
set.look_accent_why: Buttons, highlights, the lights behind the glass and the icon all follow it
set.look_scene_why: The colour of the room behind the panels
set.look_lights_why: The coloured glows drifting in the corners
set.look_grid_why: The faint square grid behind everything
set.look_reset_why: Back to slate, the accent background and a 24 px blur
changelog.title: Changelog
log.simbrief_failed: SimBrief could not be read at startup: {detail}
ob.again_why: The downloads, the microphone, the push-to-talk key and SimBrief, one screen each
ob.welcome_text: A few minutes of setup: the downloads, your microphone, a push-to-talk key and SimBrief. Everything runs on this computer.
ob.card_offline_why: Speech and voices run on this computer. No account.
ob.card_free_why: Open source, with no subscription and nothing to sign up for.
ob.card_later_why: Every choice here is in Settings afterwards.
ob.dl_text: Three pieces are too big to ship inside the program and are fetched once. The radio speaks English everywhere, and the local language where a controller works one: that follows the aeroplane, so there is no language to choose here.
ob.mic_text: Say a few words: the bar should move. A headset microphone works best.
ob.ptt_text: Hold to transmit, release to send, just like the real radio. The key works with the simulator in front.
ob.plan_text: Connect SimBrief so the controller knows your callsign, route and cruise level.
ob.plan_none: No SimBrief? Fly without it: the pencil on the flight strip takes your callsign and route by hand.
ob.ready_text: Start Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 and load your aircraft. Tune your airport's frequency in COM1, hold your push-to-talk key and make your first call.
ob.note_busy: You can carry on: the downloads keep going in the background.
ob.note: Anything here can be fetched later from Settings, Components.
ob.hint_off: Use the microphone button in the window, or type what you would say.
ob.press_button: Press the button on your yoke or stick
ob.hint_hold: Hold it while you speak, with the simulator in front.
ob.press_key: Press the key you want to use
ob.simbrief_empty: Type your SimBrief username or ID first.
ob.restart_first: Restart WilcoATC once the downloads have finished: the radio starts with them.
ob.navdata_why: Every airport, runway and frequency in the world
ob.voices_why: The voices your controllers speak with
ob.speech_why: The model that hears what you say
log.invented_frequency: No published frequency is known for {station}; {mhz} is invented. If you know the real one, please report it on GitHub.
set.controller_report_why: If your controller is missing or a button does nothing, this writes one file to attach to your report: what Windows and this program see, and the buttons you press in the next 10 seconds.
set.controller_report_running: Press every button on your controllers now — 10 seconds…
set.controller_report_failed: The report could not be written: {reason}
set.joystick_missing: Joystick support is missing from this installation. Please report it.
log.ptt_joystick_missing: Joystick support is missing from this installation. Please report it.
set.look_gradient_why: Buttons and highlights shade from one tint of the accent to another, instead of one flat colour
flight.pln_bad: That file is not a flight plan the simulator wrote.
ob.look_text: A theme and an accent colour. The window changes as you pick; the rest of the look is in Settings, Personalisation.
set.fo_card_why: The pilot in the other seat: callouts, checklists and the numbers read back on the interphone. Nothing they say goes out on the radio. The Immersion switch also turns the cabin crew on and off.
set.crew_card_why: A purser and a cabin behind you, on the address system. None of it changes what ATC says. The Immersion switch also turns the first officer on and off.
set.immersion_why: The rest of the aeroplane. A first officer in the other seat and a cabin crew behind you, following the flight the same way the controller does. None of it goes out on the radio, and none of it changes what ATC says.
ob.fo_text: Somebody in the right seat for the callouts, the checklists and the numbers read back on the interphone. Choose who, and listen before you decide.
ob.fo_on_why: Never on the radio, and it changes nothing the controller says. Everything else about them is in Settings, First officer.
ob.fo_wait: The voices are still downloading: for now you can choose a man, a woman or a cast from the aircraft, and pick a person later in Settings, First officer.
ob.fo_cannot: That voice could not be played. Have the voices finished downloading?
log.live_down: Live traffic: no source answering, invented traffic in use.
log.live_fsltl: Live traffic stays off: FSLTL flies the traffic (Settings, Traffic).
set.source_wilcoatc_why: WilcoATC: the real flights from the live feed when it is on, invented ones in the gaps. Turn FSLTL's own injector off.
set.source_fsltl_why: FSLTL: its aircraft are the traffic and the controllers work them; no live feed.
set.source_next: Takes effect at the next session.
set.traffic_live_why: The real aircraft around you, shown 30 s behind the real ones. Only your position and a radius are sent.
live.down: No source answering, invented traffic in use
update.title: A new version is out
update.check_why: Asks GitHub whether a newer version is out. Nothing is downloaded until you say yes
update.ready: Ready. WilcoATC will close and start again on the new version; your settings and voices are kept.
update.failed: The update could not be downloaded. Nothing was changed; try again later.
update.why_checkout: This copy runs from the source code: update it with git, or download the new version.
update.why_readonly: WilcoATC cannot write to its own folder, so it cannot update itself. Download the new version and unpack it over this one.
update.why_no_asset: This release has no download for this edition yet.
tb.no_stations: No published stations for this field
tb.opt_crew_sub: Callouts, checklists and the crew in the cabin
tb.opt_radio_sub: The VHF sound on every controller
tb.read_back: Read back — the controller is waiting
tb.rest_in_app: Everything else — voices, language, SimBrief — lives in the desktop app.
tb.start_it: Start it on this PC. This panel reconnects on its own.
tb.switch_why: Swap active and standby, in the aircraft too
set.radio_power_why: Cold and dark, nothing is heard and nothing goes out until the battery and the avionics are on. Turn it off for an add-on whose own electrics the simulator does not see
log.radio_off: The radio has no power: nothing is heard and nothing goes out until the battery and the avionics are on.
log.radio_no_power: The radio has no power: nothing was transmitted. Switch on the battery and the avionics.
perf.title: Performance profile
perf.normal_why: Quick: on a processor alone, a clearance arrives in about the time it takes to say it.
perf.high_why: The closest to the words, but on a processor alone a clearance takes about twice as long to arrive.
log.speech_missing: The speech recognition has not been downloaded yet. Open Settings, then Components, and press Download.
